prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To generate a real damages range, we need: (1) the unit's square footage, so the stated $275/sq ft figure can be converted into a total dollar value; (2) the actual price and terms of the 2015 Mostafavi offer that triggered the ROFR, which establishes what Shaw would have had to pay to exercise the right and is the baseline for any 'lost bargain' calculation; and (3) either a contemporaneous 2015 appraisal/valuation of the unit or expert testimony establishing its fair market value at the time of breach, since damages for a lost ROFR are typically measured as of the breach date rather than today's market.
prediction.likelyOutcome: Shaw is very likely to establish the underlying breach (A&M has effectively conceded it), but A&M's waiver/estoppel-by-acquiescence defense presents a genuine, roughly coin-flip risk given the seven-year delay, continued lease payments, and repeated renewal negotiations that never mentioned the 2015 breach. Even in a full win, damages will likely be measured at 2015 values (the actual Mostafavi offer terms) rather than Shaw's current $275/sq ft estimate, and the record as described lacks the square footage and 2015 sale-price data needed to compute an actual number.

issues.label: Breach of Right of First Refusal (liability)
Timeliness of Suit / No Statute-of-Limitations Bar

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court awarded the tenant $257,216 in damages plus post-judgment interest, using the tenant's damages methodology (unrealized appreciation, rent-versus-mortgage differential, lost principal) but valuing the unit at the $166.73 per square foot the third-party buyers paid rather than the $275 the tenant proposed. No attorney's fees. The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed (2-1) on August 19, 2026, rejecting the estoppel-by-acquiescence and failure-to-mitigate defenses.
